# The Assumptions Reference

<DoxygenPage version="1.13.2">

## Description {#details}

Assumptions represent essential preconditions that must hold true for a test case to execute meaningfully. If an assumption fails, the test is immediately terminated, as continuing would render the results invalid or misleading.

By clearly specifying assumptions, developers can ensure that tests are only run in appropriate contexts, improving the reliability and accuracy of test outcomes. This mechanism is particularly valuable for guarding against invalid input, incomplete initialisation, or unsupported environments.

### assume() {#ga0f5febbef70eb641691b98583410a1ca}

The <code>assume</code> function template evaluates a logical condition or custom expression and, if the condition is false, aborts the current test case within the µTest++ framework. This mechanism is intended for preconditions or assumptions that must hold for the test to be meaningful. If the assumption fails, the test case is terminated early and reported as skipped or failed, depending on the framework configuration.

The function template can be used with any expression that evaluates to a boolean or with custom comparators/operators derived from the local <code>detail::op</code> type. It returns an output stream, allowing optional messages to be appended to the test report for diagnostic purposes.
